column2: How do I install the full weather pack or the Europe pack?
column3: The pack is built (or downloaded) once, on any computer with the Internet: step-by-step instructions in docs/METEO.md (program scripts/meteo/build-meteo.py). Then, Settings → “🌦 Weather of the past” → “⤒ Import the file…”: the “Import” window checks the .lcmeteo file, shows what will come in (stations, years, hours, size), then imports it, with “↶ Undo”. The base set stays: the pack is added on top. “🗑 Delete the pack” removes it (with “↶ Undo”). “↗ About the data” gives each source and its licence. The Europe pack adds stations in Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, the United Kingdom, Spain, Poland and Czechia (and a few long series from Italy, Portugal and Slovakia), and, for all of Europe, the 20CR reconstruction (1836–1939) and ERA5: every place in Europe then has at least a “Rough reconstruction” before 1940. To build it, you sometimes need a free key (AEMET for Spain, CEDA for the United Kingdom): docs/METEO.md explains everything; a source without a key is simply skipped.

column2: Where can I see the weather other than on the record?
column3: The “🌦 Weather of their life” block on the record (to switch on in the weather settings: each big day of the life, and curious sentences such as “Born during the coldest week of the winter of 1900–1901 in Agen”); the “🌦 Weather of the past” widget on the dashboard (“100 years ago, on the day Jean and Marie married, it was raining in Auch”) and the ancestors’ badges in “🎂 Dates to celebrate”; Timeline → “🌦 Weather” in the column; the page layout → Object menu → “🌦 Weather box for an event…” (a dynamic object, with its source). Never a living person or a confidential record in the widget.

column2: How do I track animals (rings, microchips, GPS collars, sightings)?
column3: Switch on the “🐾 Animal tracking” tab: Settings → Appearance → Top tabs (it is hidden at first), or “↗ Show the tab” in the list of animals. Its page is made of blocks like the dashboard: map of sightings, latest sightings, tracked animals, today’s GPS track, figures, counts at a site, animals to find, search by ring or chip, GPS import, weather, veterinary follow-up, groups. You can also put the usual dashboard widgets there (left column, “Other widgets of the app” section).

column2: How do I have a tracking page per species?
column3: In Tracking, “＋ New page”: its name, its icon, the species and the site. The page starts from blocks suggested for this species and only shows its animals (a block can keep its own choice with ✎). The page’s ⋯ (or a right-click on its button): rename, change the icon, duplicate, page shown on opening, delete (↶ Undo).

column2: How do I put a tracking block on the dashboard?
column3: The block’s ⋯ → “📌 Also put it on the dashboard”: it is copied with its settings to the “Overview” page. The tracking blocks are also in the dashboard column, in the “🐾 Animal tracking” section, and work even if the tab is hidden.

column2: How do I note a bird’s colour rings?
column3: The animal’s record → “🔖 Rings and marks” block (section of the same name) → “🎨 Colour rings” → ✎: click one of the 4 positions (left or right leg, top or bottom), then one of the basic ring colours (white, black, red, orange, yellow, light green, dark green, light blue, dark blue, purple, pink, grey, brown, metal) or “Other colour” (the shared colour window: eyedropper, # code, recent colours), and the engraved code. A change keeps the old combination in the history.

column2: Which marks are offered depending on the species?
column3: Bird: metal ring, colour rings, wing tag, GPS tag. Cat, dog: microchip, tattoo, collar, tag, GPS collar. Horse: microchip, UELN, description. Cow, sheep: ear tag, tattoo. Fish, turtle, bat: PIT, scute mark, forearm ring, transmitter. Marine animal: photo-identification (fin, fluke, scars), Argos tag, fin tag, PIT. Wild mammal: GPS or VHF collar, ear tag, ear notch, tattoo, microchip, photo-identification. Primate: photo-identification, microchip, tattoo. Everywhere: “Other mark”.

column2: I misread a ring code: how do I say so?
column3: In “New sighting”, write “?” for a character you could not read (“7?”) and [K|X] when you are unsure (“7[K|X]”, “3[3|8]”). Or click a character: sure → not read → “I’m unsure between…”. The app looks for the matching animals, with a lower score for doubtful characters, and the sighting keeps the reading: “reading: 7[K|X] (doubt)” with the “Partial reading” badge.

column2: How do I find an animal seen outdoors?
column3: “＋ New sighting”: for a bird, click the colours seen on the legs (“?” = colour not sure, “∅” = no ring) and the code read; for a cat, a dog, a cow, a marine animal… the number read, even partly (“250 26 9…”). The app suggests the most likely animals (colours, code, seen near here) with a percentage. Otherwise: “＋ Create the record of a new animal” or “✎ Keep without a record”. A sighting can have several photos, sounds or videos (“Photos, sounds or videos” box): you see them as small thumbnails (3, then “+N”) in lists, blocks and the map; a click shows them large, one after the other.

column2: How do I import the track of a GPS tag or collar?
column3: “⤒ Import a track…” (Tracking, the animal’s record, or the “Quick GPS import” block): GPX, KML, GeoJSON, CSV (Movebank export, Tractive, Weenect, Invoxia, Kippy collars…). Step 2: the number of points, “one every N min”, “split into nights”, the animal (suggested automatically if the tag is on its record). Afterwards “↶ Undo” removes the points.

column2: Where can I see the health of an animal in care?
column3: The “🩺 Health” tab of its record: the timeline of states (healthy, injured, ill, in care, released, dead), the weight curve and each event (what it has, why, where, who treated it, care, medicines, weight, photos, outcome). The “🩺 Veterinary follow-up and state” block shows all the animals at a glance, with the most frequent causes of injury.

column2: How do I note that an animal belongs to a pack, a troop or a pod?
column3: The “👥 Group” tab of its record: “＋ Joined a group” (the group, its role: alpha, matriarch, young, satellite… or a free word, the date). Then “Change role” or “Left the group…” (gone, excluded, dead, moved to another group). The timeline shows its whole social history; the group page shows its current and past members.

column2: Where can I see all the animals and all the sightings?
column3: Lists → “🐾 Census” (also in the Tracking ⋯): Sightings, Tracked animals, Sites, Groups tabs; the shared bar (search, filter by species, site, year, ring reading…), List or Cards, sort. “⤓ Export ▾”: CSV, Movebank, GPX, KML or “🧾 Open in the spreadsheet”.

column2: How do I share my animal tracking with someone?
column3: In Tracking (⋯), the Census or an animal’s record: “📤 Share”: one record, chosen animals, a species, a site or all the tracking, with or without the GPS points and the photos. The observers’ names only go if you tick the box. The other person opens it with “⤒ Receive shared tracking…”: they see what will come in, then compare and choose for each difference (mine, theirs, both) before merging; “↶ Undo” puts everything back as before.

column2: How do I check that there are no mistakes in my database?
column3: Settings → Data quality → “✅ Database check”: a single list of what seems impossible or very rare (born after the father’s death, married after their own death, a 57-year-old mother, 31 February, duplicates, misplaced places, impossible journeys, baptism far from the place of birth, burial before death, sex that does not match the Sosa number, “between 1900 and 1800” written backwards, a date that is too long (a note pasted into it), “-5” read as the year 5, a person married to their grandson or to their ancestor, an animal recorded as a person’s parent or spouse…). The “Merge duplicates” list shows the same duplicates, with the same number. Badges 📅 Dates, 🎂 Ages, 👪 Parents, 👥 Duplicates, 📍 Places and 🔴 🟠 🟡 with the number found; “Filter ▾” for a branch, your ancestors (Sosa) or someone’s descendants; “⤓ CSV” to work at the archives. On each line: “↗ Record” (the child and the parent), “✎ Fix” (opens the event concerned) and “This is not a mistake”. Nothing is changed without you.

column2: A check alert is wrong: how do I stop seeing it?
column3: “This is not a mistake”: choose a reason (“I checked in the record”, “These are two different people”, “The place is right”…), add a note if you like, then “Stop reporting” (“↶ Undo” right after). It goes into the “🙈 Exceptions” badge, from where “↺ Report again” brings it back. If one of the dates concerned changes later, the alert comes back by itself, marked “Dates changed” (box ticked automatically). Two different people are no longer suggested in “Merge duplicates” either.

column2: I am merging two records that each have their own parents: what happens?
column3: The record you keep receives both families of parents (nothing is deleted). Before merging, “⚖️ Compare” (Settings → Merge duplicates) says so in a yellow ⚠️ box, and so does the question before the merge. Afterwards, the “✅ Database check” points out the record with two families of parents: open it and remove (“Remove”) the wrong family.

column2: How do I go through the check alerts one by one?
column3: In “✅ Database check”, “▶ One by one”: the alert in large, a small timeline of the dates, the family alongside. Dates are corrected on the spot (write them as in the record, Enter to save) and the alert is recalculated straight away. On the keyboard: C fix, N not a mistake, L later, ← → previous / next, Esc to go back to the list.

column2: Can I change the age from which a mother is flagged as “too old”?
column3: Yes: Settings → “⚙️ Check thresholds”: age of the mother and of the father (to check 🟠 / impossible 🔴), young marriage, longevity, delay after the father’s death, gap between two births, distant baptism, likeness of duplicates… Each slider is saved straight away (“↶ Undo” in the message), double-click = starting value, “↺ Reset to default” at the top. You also choose the record banner there: always, only 🔴 or never.

column2: What does “⚠️ 2 things to check” at the top of a record mean?
column3: It is the database check banner: what seems impossible for this person (“Married on 17 April 1863, after his death”, “His daughter Louise is born 4 years after his death”). It is folded: “See ▾” unfolds it, with “✎ Fix” and “Not a mistake”. An alert set aside does not come back there. The “✅ Database check” widget on the dashboard gives the number by kind and the % of records without an alert.

column2: Why are shortcuts not written the same on a Mac and on a PC?
column3: Shortcuts are written for your computer: the Command key on a Mac, Ctrl on Windows and Linux, as small grey keys, the same everywhere (tooltips, menus, texts and Settings → Keyboard shortcuts). Leave the mouse on a button for a moment: a black tooltip says what it is for, with its key.
